chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahboub from Jameel ibn Salih from Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira Al-Nadri from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever hears the Mu'adhdhin saying, 'I testify that there is no god except Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,' and he says, affirming and anticipating (reward), 'And I testify that there is no god except Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family),' and he suffices with these two (testimonies) from those who refused and denied, and he is aided by these two (testimonies) [for] whoever acknowledges and testifies, there is for him from the reward the number of those who denied and rejected, and the like of the number of those who acknowledged and recognized.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for responding to the Adhan with the testimony of faith?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith underscores the communal nature of the Adhan, where the listener’s affirmation acts as a spiritual counterweight to both denial and affirmation. Scholars highlight the 'multiplication of reward' mechanism, suggesting that the listener shares in the merit of every individual who recites the Shahada, thereby amplifying the collective witness to Tawhid and Nubuwwah. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the Mu'adhdhin’s role as a public announcer whose call generates continuous, distributed reward for the community.
